test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: An order was placed for the supply of a carpet whose breadth was 6 m and whose length were 1.44 times the breadth. What is the cost of a carpet whose length and breadth are 40% more and 25% more respectively than the first carpet. [The cost of a carpet is Rs. 45 per sq m.]
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

New **Area** = Old **Area** × (1 + % increase in **length**) × (1 + % increase in **breadth**)

Old **Area** = 6 × (1.44 × 6) = 51.84 m²

New **Area** = 51.84 × 1.40 × 1.25 = 51.84 × 1.75 = 90.72 m²

Total **Cost** = 90.72 × 45 = ₹4082.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4082.40.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First carpet **breadth** (B₁) = 6 m

First carpet **length** (L₁) = 1.44 × 6 = 8.64 m

Rate of **carpet** = ₹45 per sq m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3d7daf7606f501799b4a1728531936918024051fab661d0639de90ca1221c3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Breadth** of second carpet (B₂) = 6 + (25% of 6) = 6 × 1.25 = 7.5 m

⇒ **Length** of second carpet (L₂) = 8.64 + (40% of 8.64) = 8.64 × 1.4 = 12.096 m

⇒ **Area** of second carpet = L₂ × B₂

⇒ **Area** = 12.096 × 7.5 = 90.72 m²

⇒ Total **Cost** = **Area** × Rate

⇒ Total **Cost** = 90.72 × 45

⇒ Total **Cost** = ₹4082.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4082.40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by a **rectangle** is given by the formula: Area = **Length** × **Breadth**.

Successive Percentage Increase

If two dimensions are increased by a% and b%, the resultant **area** increases by [a + b + (a×b)/100]%. In this case: 40 + 25 + (40×25)/100 = 75% total increase.

Unitary Method for Cost

Total **Cost** = (Total **Quantity**/**Area**) × (Rate per unit **Quantity**/**Area**).
